messages.author: e53f91d0708becab
messages.subject: my.symbols(ms.arrows) in ggplot
parts:
Any chance to get arrows in ggplot build as my.symbols(ms.arrows) from
TeachingDemos?
Using angle and lenght seems to be far more interesting and much more
aplicable than origin-destination, as geom_segment() works.

messages.author: 5a1b5a9591c118ef
messages.subject: Re: my.symbols(ms.arrows) in ggplot
parts:
Hi,

I started writing a new geom for this purpose last year. It's pretty
rough, especially with the legend, but maybe it can give you some
inspiration.

library(ggExtra) # r-forge
d <- diamonds[sample(nrow(diamonds), 100), ]
p <- ggplot(d, aes(carat, price, colour=cut))
p + geom_field(aes(angle=carat), length=0.1, arrow=arrow())

HTH,

baptiste

messages.subject: log2 scale problem
parts:
To ggplot2 workers,

I'm attempting to put a log2 scale on the x-axis and get an error message I
don't understand.

I have a dataframe with 6 variables.

> names(movePain.df)
[1] "id" "anesthetic" "variable" "moveVAS" "hour"
"logitMoveVAS"


This command produces the expected dot plot:

ggplot(movePain.df, aes(hour, moveVAS, group = hour)) + scale_x_log2() +
geom_jitter() + facet_wrap(~ anesthetic, ncol = 3)

This command produces the expected box plot:

ggplot(movePain.df, aes(hour, moveVAS, group = hour)) + geom_boxplot() +
facet_wrap(~ anesthetic, ncol = 3)

However, when I attempt to log2 scale the x axis for a box plot I get an
error message:

ggplot(movePain.df, aes(hour, moveVAS, group = hour)) + scale_x_log2() +
geom_boxplot() + facet_wrap(~ anesthetic, ncol = 3)
Error in if (any(diff(intervals) < -1e-06)) { :
missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed

For each of the three plots I do get a warning message about missing values:

Either

Warning messages:
1: Removed 2 rows containing missing values (geom_point).
2: Removed 1 rows containing missing values (geom_point).

Or

Warning messages:
1: Removed 2 rows containing missing values (stat_boxplot).
2: Removed 1 rows containing missing values (stat_boxplot).

My session info is below.

Comments will be appreciated.

Nathan

messages.author: e53f91d0708becab
messages.subject: Re: my.symbols(ms.arrows) in ggplot
parts:
Ok,

I manage to manipulate stat_spoke parameters to get the desired graph.
As an example

rads <- data.frame("ang" = 0:360)
for(i in 0:360){
rads[i+1,2] <- circ.mean(rad(i))
}
rads$deg <- CircStats::deg(rads$V2)
rads$degNum <- formatC(rads$deg)
rads$degNum[361] <- "-1"
rads$radc <- format(rads$V2, sci = F)
rads$class_ang <- cut(rads$ang, breaks=c(0, 45, 90, 135, 180, 225,
270, 315, 360.1),
include.lowest = T, right = F, labels = c("0-45", "45-90", "90-135",
"135-180",
"180-225", "225-270", "270-315", "315-360"))
rads$x <- expand.grid(1:19,1:19)$Var1
rads$y <- expand.grid(19:1,19:1)$Var2
gr <- ggplot(data = rads, aes(x = x,y = y)) + geom_point(size=0.01,
alpha=0.1)
gr + geom_text(aes(label = rads$ang, size=4),hjust = 0, vjust = 0)+
stat_spoke(aes(angle=V2), radius = 0.5, arrow = arrow(length =
unit(0.1, "inches"))) #+ geom_text(label = degNum)

I'm not being able to correctly manipulate deg-rad angles but the
example above works as an example of stat_spoke() use

messages.author: 2ce42083844457dd
messages.subject: Equivalent parameter to xyplot argument index.cond
parts:
Hi All,

In lattice there is an argument index.cond used in xyplot to arrange the
order of the panels.

"Another possibility is to specify index.cond as a function. In this case,
this function is called once for each panel, potentially with all arguments
that are passed to the panel function for that panel. (More specifically, if
this function has a ... argument, then all panel arguments are passed,
otherwise, only named arguments that match are passed.) For a single
conditioning variable, the levels of that variable are then sorted so that
these values are in ascending order. For multiple conditioning variables,
the order for each variable is determined by first taking the average over
all other conditioning variables."

I've looked at the book, the help pages, and the website. I need help
finding an equivalent in ggplot2 for setting the order of the plots in
facet_wrap by a function of the data in each plot of the facet ribbon.

Nathan

messages.subject: Re: Equivalent parameter to xyplot argument index.cond
parts:
Hi:

It sounds as though the reorder() function might be useful in this context. For example, in Figure 11.2 of the Lattice book, state.name is reordered by Frost value in order to get the 'increasing response' appearance in each panel. In this case, however, it seems that you want to reorder factor levels by some (summary) measure and then apply that reordering to the factor levels in order to influence panel placement order with facet_wrap() or facet_grid(). You can do the calculations and reordering before plotting by creating a new factor with level order determined by reorder() for each desired factor and then use the reordered factors in the ggplot. I don't think there is a facility within the faceting functions themselves to do this on the fly within a ggplot() call. I'm sure that Hadley or another ggplot2 guru will chime in if I'm in error on this point.

BTW, that section of the xyplot help page also says:
"Although they can be supplied in high level function calls directly, it is more typical to use perm.cond and index.cond to update an existing "trellis" object, thus allowing it to be displayed in a different arrangement without re-calculating the data subsets that go into each panel. In the update method, both can be set to NULL, which reverts these back to their defaults."

...which rather suggests to me that the ordering can be determined by external means before being applied to the graphic object.

HTH,
Dennis
